name: Flux Vole
description: The Flux Vole is a small rodent, 15 to 20 centimeters body length, descended from the prairie vole strains that colonized GLMZ's interior districts as agricultural land was absorbed into the megacity's sprawl. It is distinguished from its ancestors by a dramatically altered skin physiology: the Flux Vole's outer dermal layer has become highly resistant to electrical current through a combination of thickened, lipid-dense skin and a specialized subcutaneous fat layer that provides insulation. This adaptation emerged over roughly eight generations of selection among populations nesting within active electrical conduit housings and transformer substations. Externally, the Flux Vole appears almost normal — small, rounded, with short buff-brown fur — except that its fur tends to stand slightly erect even at rest, a side effect of the static charge that builds up in its coat from contact with live infrastructure. In darkness, a disturbed Flux Vole will briefly produce small visible static discharges from its fur, a phenomenon that gave rise to its street name.
diet: Seeds, insects, insulation material, fungal growth on conduit interior surfaces, condensation-moisture from pipe exteriors
notable_traits: Dramatically thickened, electrically insulating dermal layer
Static charge accumulation in fur — produces visible micro-discharges when disturbed
Nests successfully inside active electrical conduit and transformer housings
Subcutaneous fat layer provides thermal insulation as secondary adaptation
encounters: Flux Voles are most often encountered by utility workers and illegal infrastructure tappers accessing transformer substations or conduit runs. They scatter when disturbed, and a panicked Flux Vole running across a live electrical surface produces a brief light show of static discharge that has startled more than one worker into a dangerous reflex. They are otherwise harmless. Children in districts adjacent to substations sometimes collect them as pets, though their slightly bristled fur and the faint static tingle of handling them unsettles some people.
known_uses: Occasionally kept as pets in Tier 1 households — their docile temperament and the novelty of their static display makes them mildly popular. Some Tier 1 folk medicine holds that the fat layer of a Flux Vole, rendered and applied, is effective against minor electrical burns — there is no credible evidence for this. Helix Biosystems researchers have expressed interest in the dermal insulation mechanism as a basis for human biomod applications.
story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems procurement agent is paying unusually well for live Flux Voles in quantity — more than the novelty pet market justifies. Someone is running a collection operation through Tier 1 kids, and the agent's actual research purpose is not what they've stated.

A transformer substation that should be decommissioned has an enormous Flux Vole colony living inside it — and the colony's presence is somehow keeping a jury-rigged power connection alive for a Tier 1 community that officially has no power access.
